title: Why You Suddenly See Your Nose, Even Though It's Always There
hook: You are seeing your nose right now, aren't you?

narration.text: Your brain constantly edits out your nose from your vision.
It considers this stationary image unimportant background noise.
But if you think about it, your brain starts to notice it again.
This is called unconscious selective attention.
It helps us focus on important things, ignoring the constant input.
Now, try to ignore your nose. It is very difficult.
Try it right now and tell me if it worked on you in the comments, and like this if it surprised you.

description: Have you ever wondered why you suddenly notice your nose in your field of vision, even though it's always there? It's a fascinating example of how our brains filter out constant, unchanging sensory input to help us focus on what's important.
topic: Why you suddenly notice your nose in your vision, even though it is always there. You can try to ignore it, but your brain now sees it.
